## What the data says
- Thin fabric runs nearest the Orion atmosphere (20.7-21.6 % O₂, 101.3 kPa, 5-20 cm/s flow) all sustained burning; 8 / 8 runs sustained, distance-weighted share 100 % [PSI-25][PSI-98].
- Evidence coverage for thin fabric at these conditions is 0.986 (high proximity of test points) [PSI-25][PSI-98].
- Physics estimate (adiabatic flame temperature ≈ 2270 K) is ~50 K below the hottest thin-fabric microgravity test (≈ 2320 K) and ~260 K above the coldest burning test (≈ 2010 K) [PSI-25][PSI-98].
- Thin solid (films, sheets) runs at 21 % O₂, 101.3 kPa, 1-10 cm/s flow show 7 / 8 sustained, 1 marginal; distance-weighted share 93.8 % [PSI-25].
- Evidence coverage for thin solid is 1.0 [PSI-25].
- Thick solid runs at similar conditions show 8 / 8 sustained, share 100 % [PSI-25]; coverage 0.989.
- Liquid-fuel droplet runs (methanol) at 21 % O₂, 101-101.9 kPa, 0 cm/s flow: 8 / 8 sustained, share 100 % [PSI-69].
- Fire-resistant materials: Nomex - 3 / 4 runs sustained; Silicone - 0 / 4 runs sustained; total 3 / 8 sustained, 5 / 8 extinguished at ≤ 22.2 % O₂ [PSI-25][PSI-99].
- NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 failure for Nomex HT90-40 at 30 % O₂, 70.1 kPa in 1 g reported (NTRS 20070018178).
- Partial-gravity data are absent; lunar or Martian gravity may be more hazardous than both micro- and Earth-gravity (NTRS 20260000646).

## How confident we can be
- Confidence for thin fabric is the evidence coverage value 0.986; for thin solid it is 1.0; for thick solid 0.989 [PSI-25].
- Solid data limitation: 131 / 134 solid runs sustained, only 2 extinction-velocity limits and 1 no-ignition run, so a flammability limit cannot be located [PSI-25][PSI-98][PSI-99].
- Fire-resistant material confidence is low; only 8 runs total, mixed outcomes, and no predictor estimate provided [PSI-25][PSI-99].
- Droplet data confidence is high (coverage = 1) for methanol at the target atmosphere [PSI-69].

## Gaps
- No microgravity tests for thin fabric at oxygen levels below 20 % or at different flow speeds; no extinction-velocity limits for this class.
- No partial-gravity (lunar, Martian) combustion data for any material class; behavior may differ from both micro- and 1-g results.
- Fire-resistant materials lack sufficient runs to define oxygen limits; silicone and Nomex were not tested at higher O₂ concentrations.
- No solid-material tests with oxygen > 22.2 % to bound upper flammability.
- No data on heat-loss effects, material chemistry variations, or different ventilation rates for thin fabric.

## What future experiments (e.g. LUCI, FM2) should measure
- Thin fabric droplet or sheet burns at O₂ < 20 % and at multiple flow velocities to capture extinction-velocity limits.
- Partial-gravity flame spread tests for thin fabric, thin solid, and fire-resistant fabrics to assess hazard in lunar/Martian gravity.
- Extended oxygen range (up to 30 % O₂) for silicone and Nomex to locate flammability limits and validate NASA-STD-6001 findings.
- Controlled heat-loss experiments (varying ventilation) for thin fabric to separate flow and radiative effects.
- High-oxygen (≥ 25 % O₂) solid runs to define upper bound of sustained burning for thin and thick solids.
